scope: Classic Normal only; optional compile guard AI_BELIEF_PRIORS; no saved strength result yet
hypothesis: Posterior Flag/Bomb probabilities should guide persistent native targets and quiet routing, rather than only adding an immediate capture correction after native move evaluation.

source.title: Kaelbling, Littman and Cassandra (1998), Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
source.basis: Belief-state immediate reward is the expectation of state reward. Applying this to native heuristic combat gains is an approximation, not a claim of optimal planning.

mechanism.state: Two 100-entry uint16 Q12 arrays and one owner/valid byte (401 bytes).
mechanism.validation: Setter transactionally rejects null arrays, invalid army, values above 4096, or square-wise Flag+Bomb probability above 4096. Reset clears arrays and validity.
mechanism.owner: Army 0 (Red) or 16 (Blue); owner prevents another army using stale priors. Caller refreshes before each decision.
integration: plan(): target expected gain for each concealed enemy
score(): immediate expected gain for a concealed capture before existing nonlinear guards
mechanism.expectation: [H*(qFlag*2000 + qBomb*gain(a,Bomb)) + (4096-qFlag-qBomb)*sum_r(hidden[r]*gain(a,r))]/(4096*H), with one final signed truncating division; H is remaining hidden mobile population.
mechanism.moved: A publicly moved target retains existing mobile-only expectation regardless of supplied immobile mass.
mechanism.no_mobile: With H=0, use immobile expectation only if qFlag+qBomb=4096; otherwise fall back to original expectation.
mechanism.preserved: No board disclosure changes; revealed targets, immediate known wins, other difficulties and optional rules retain existing treatment. Existing danger, rank-discovery, near-own-Flag and goal utility transforms still apply.
mechanism.behavioral_likelihood: Mobile rank probabilities are exchangeable remaining inventory; approach/retreat rank likelihoods deliberately omitted.

quiet_fixture.interpretation: Demonstrates belief-to-objective-to-action linkage; does not estimate playing strength.

checks: Macro-off ELF byte parity against immutable frozen student-guard-v1-normal sources and recipe
Exact rational expected-gain parity for counts and joint marginal fixtures
Concealed enemy rank nibble permutations preserve goals, expected values and move
Invalid setter leaves state unchanged and reset clears entire appended state
Save/load restores prior owner, arrays and original native memory
Wrong owner, Easy and Hard use original expectations
Quiet target and move change without disclosure changes

limits: Q12 discretizes probabilities; setter enforces numeric bounds, while public model code owns inventory consistency.
Single-piece native goals and existing heuristic nonlinearities remain; this is not a full belief-state search.
Better routing can still chase unlikely Flags or underweight cooperative trades; strength requires registered immutable paired Classic evaluation.
